title: Distributed Erlang Core: Nodes, Magic Cookies, rpc:call & pg Groups
solutionExplanation: Integrates distributed Erlang RPC with OTP 23+ decentralized pg process groups.

otpDocCards.signature: rpc:call(Node, Module, Function, Args, Timeout) -> Res | {badrpc, Reason}
otpDocCards.description: Evaluates apply(Module, Function, Args) on Node and returns the corresponding value, or {badrpc, Reason} if the call fails.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Synchronous network message roundtrip with timeout.

otpDocCards.description: Subscribes one or more processes to a distributed process group across the cluster.
Returns all live process identifiers currently joined to the specified group.
Unsubscribes one or more processes from the group.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why was pg introduced in OTP 23 to replace the legacy pg2 module?

options.label: pg uses raw UDP packets instead of TCP for cluster routing.
options.explanation: pg uses standard BEAM distributed node distribution channels over TCP/TLS.

options.label: pg2 had a single central coordinator process per node, creating a bottleneck; pg uses a decentralized, lock-free architecture.
options.explanation: pg was designed to replace pg2 because pg2 suffered from a single centralized coordinator process that created message bottlenecks at scale. pg is fully decentralized and lock-free.

options.label: pg2 required nodes to share a physical hard drive to coordinate subscriptions.
options.explanation: Neither pg nor pg2 requires shared disk storage.

options.label: pg encrypts all message payloads with AES-256 by default.
options.explanation: Distribution encryption is handled at the Erlang distribution layer, not by pg.
